citations.anchor: is omitted while no workspace is open
citations.why: Drives the shipped interceptor stack with no workspace set and asserts the captured request header is `undefined` — an empty-string header would fail it.

citations.anchor: carries the active workspace once one is opened, and stops when it is cleared
citations.why: Asserts the header is the active id on two requests and gone again after setActiveWorkspaceId(null).

citations.anchor: does not exempt the prefix-sharing path %s
citations.why: A 401 on /auth/logins-report, /auth/invites-admin, /auth/meta and /auth/logout-all must still fire the handler — a bare startsWith would exempt all four and fail this.

citations.anchor: still exempts %s when the caller omits the leading slash
citations.why: Pins the normalization half: matching the caller-passed string rather than the normalized path drops 'auth/login' out of the exemption list and fires the handler.

citations.anchor: rethrows the original 401 even if the handler throws
citations.why: Installs a throwing handler and asserts the caller's rejection is still the AxiosError with response.status 401.

citations.anchor: reports a transport failure as status null with no details
citations.why: An AxiosError with no `response` normalizes to status null; any invented numeric status fails the assertion.

citations.anchor: retries a transport failure with no response at all
citations.why: Pins the second half — the shipped retry predicate reads status === null as the retryable no-response case.

citations.anchor: does not retry the settled client error %i
citations.why: The shipped predicate returns false for 400/401/403/404/409/418/422/499; a retried 4xx fails it.

citations.anchor: retries the transient client error %i
citations.why: Pins the two exemptions: 408 and 429 return true.

citations.anchor: gives up after three attempts even on a retryable failure
citations.why: failureCount 2 retries and 3 does not, pinning the at-most-three cap; the sibling 5xx case pins that server errors are retried.

citations.anchor: does not let a consumer mutate the slot through the returned array
citations.why: Pushes, sorts and truncates the array getItems() returned, then asserts a fresh read is unchanged — handing back the live array fails it.

citations.anchor: is idempotent — running it again does not double anything
citations.why: Runs wireSlotContributions three times with the same input and asserts one item; a bare push loop yields three.

citations.anchor: does not drop an earlier contribution to the same slot
citations.why: Three contributions to one slot must all survive — folding the reset into the registration loop leaves one and fails the length assertion.

citations.anchor: sorts ascending into a new array, leaving the source untouched
citations.why: Asserts the source array's order is unchanged and that the result is not the same reference.

citations.anchor: keeps the guard armed for a second form that is still dirty
citations.why: After confirming one form's departure, isDirty is still true and the next navigation still opens the dialog — clearing the whole key set fails both.

citations.anchor: leaves React Router its history index after a confirmed navigation
citations.why: Asserts history.state.idx increments by one and stays a number across the next navigation; a raw pushState + synthetic popstate wipes the router's index and yields NaN.

citations.anchor: degrades to no guard outside a provider instead of throwing
citations.why: Renders a component using both hooks with no provider and asserts it does not throw and useUnsavedChangesApi() is null.

citations.anchor: does not compound when the page title changes underneath it
citations.why: With a decorator installed, two successive setDocumentTitle calls must give one '(3) ' prefix over the freshly composed title; appending to document.title stacks it and fails.

citations.anchor: still rejects unknown fields via the leaf resolver
citations.why: A field not declared in schema.fields raises FILTER_UNKNOWN_FIELD (a FilterException, i.e. 400) rather than reaching the translator.

citations.anchor: is unreachable at the translator too, if a tree is hand-built
citations.why: Pins the relations half at the second entry point: applyFilterTree on a hand-built tree naming an undeclared relation rejects with 'unknown relation' instead of silently dropping the predicate.

citations.anchor: rejects "${name}" with FILTER_UNKNOWN_FIELD
citations.why: Seven Object.prototype members as leaf field names must each raise FILTER_UNKNOWN_FIELD; a bare map[name] lookup resolves them truthy and fails every case.

citations.anchor: rejects "${name}.key" with FILTER_UNKNOWN_RELATION
citations.why: The same names as a mid-path relation segment must raise FILTER_UNKNOWN_RELATION, pinning the own() guard on the relations map too.

citations.anchor: rejects null instead of searching for the text "null"
citations.why: value: null on a string field raises FILTER_INVALID_VALUE; a String(v) fallback would coerce it to 'null' and pass.

citations.anchor: rejects an object and an array
citations.why: {} and [1,2] both raise FILTER_INVALID_VALUE rather than becoming '[object Object]' and '1,2'.

citations.anchor: rejects a missing `value` key instead of searching for "undefined"
citations.why: Pins the missing-key clause: a leaf with no `value` raises FILTER_INVALID_VALUE with 'value is required'.

citations.anchor: rejects ilike on %s (a %s field) instead of 500ing out of the driver
citations.why: ilike against date/number/boolean/uuid fields raises FILTER_OPERATOR_NOT_ALLOWED at 400 — the vocabulary check alone would accept all four.

citations.anchor: reports the operator rather than a value the operator never had a use for
citations.why: Pins the ordering clause: '%2020%' is not a valid date either, so the message naming the operator proves the type/operator check runs before coercion.

citations.anchor: rewrites `is none of` on a many-to-many into NOT EXISTS + IN
citations.why: Asserts the fragment starts with 'not exists' and contains the POSITIVE 'in (' and never 'not in (' — EXISTS(... NOT p ...) fails both. The 'outermost hop' clause is now pinned by its sibling 'wraps the OUTERMOST hop of a multi-hop path', which negates author.company.name and asserts exactly one 'not exists' with both the nested hop and the leaf left positive.

citations.anchor: `ne` also matches a NULL column
citations.why: The emitted fragment must contain both '<>' and '"title" is null'; a plain ne drops the NULL branch and fails.

citations.anchor: ANDs the scope predicate inside a many-to-one EXISTS
citations.why: The serialized EXISTS subquery carries the scope's workspace_id and deleted_at predicates alongside the rule's ilike.

citations.anchor: forces the m2m target join when a scope is present, even for id-only
citations.why: Pins the second clause directly, with its sibling 'keeps the m2m junction-only fast path when no scope is set' proving the fast path exists to be disabled.

citations.anchor: binds a nested many-to-one FK to the alias, not the outer table
citations.why: The nested EXISTS must correlate to "qb_parent"."author_id" and never to "content_page"."author_id" — an unrebound parent column fails both assertions.

citations.anchor: binds a nested one-to-many parentKey to the alias
citations.why: Pins both clauses at once: parentKey rebinds to the alias while the target fk stays on "content_comment", so rebinding the fk too breaks the asserted equality.

citations.anchor: translates to a now()-relative comparison, not a baked-in cutoff
citations.why: Asserts the rendered SQL contains make_interval but NOT the literal '90' — the window size is a bound parameter, never interpolated.

citations.anchor: emits the unit the caller asked for
citations.why: Only minutes/hours/days render, and the sibling 'rejects an unknown unit' 400s anything else — pinning the switch over three constants rather than a raw unit.

citations.anchor: a field declaring an unrecognised scalar type
citations.why: The coercion switch's default: throws FilterSchemaException rather than returning undefined.

citations.anchor: a relation declaring an unrecognised kind
citations.why: Goes through expectSchemaError, which asserts FilterSchemaException, status 500, code FILTER_SCHEMA_INVALID and explicitly not a FilterException — an undefined fall-through would drop the predicate instead.

citations.anchor: rejects an empty `in` list (would match no rows)
citations.why: op 'in' with [] raises FILTER_EMPTY_IN_LIST instead of reaching inArray(col, []) as SQL false.

citations.anchor: rejects an empty `nin` list (would match every row)
citations.why: The mirror clause: an empty nin raises FILTER_EMPTY_IN_LIST rather than emitting SQL true.

citations.anchor: does not let context overwrite the four reserved keys
citations.why: Builds a FilterException with context keys named code/statusCode/error/message and asserts the envelope's own values survive — spreading context last fails it.

utils:I-12.reason: Not a wrong observable — genuinely unobservable, and the module closes the one loophole itself. A violating `_reset` would have to rebind `items` (`let items = []`), and `getItems`/`_register` close over the *binding* rather than a snapshot (packages/utils/admin/src/lib/slot/index.ts:52-62), so both would immediately read and write the new array: every sequence of slot operations returns the same values under either implementation. The obvious escape — hold the array `getItems()` returned across a `_reset` and see whether it emptied — is closed by `getItems: () => items.slice()`, which hands out a copy precisely so a consumer cannot mutate shared plugin state. So there is no reference, inside the module or out, that a rebinding could leave stale. The statement's own rationale ('otherwise the closures stay on the old one') describes a capture-by-value that JavaScript closures do not do; `length = 0` is still the right code, for the ordinary reason that it is what the doc comment says, and only review enforces it.
